doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
title: Returning to New Orleans in 1930 and the Madisonville boat band
summary: De De took Buddy Petit's place on the boat; they recall Reuben Oliver, the Nelsons and Willis.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: So, then you came back. What year was it you came back to New Orleans, huh?
I came to New Orleans and, I came back to New Orleans in 30. And that's when you started working with PQ.

Yeah. Where was Buddy Petit working? Did we get that down on the table? Well, Buddy Petit was on the boat. He was on the boat. Yeah, he was on the boat. That's when I was saying I came from Birmingham and I had to wait. Which boat was that?

Madison boat we was talking about just now. Madisonville? Steaming Madison. Yeah. Madisonville. Yeah. Madisonville. Yeah. That's what I was saying. That's what I was saying. That's what I was saying. That's what I was saying.

That's what I was saying. I see. I worked there. I went right out there. After Buddy left and went over to Lake, and worked regular over there on a regular job, I was taking Buddy's place on the boat with Sadie. I went to work right now. You took Buddy's place, huh?
I took Buddy's place, huh? Same guys in the band pretty much?
Almost about the same line up.
Same bunch. Such as? I mean. Oh, no. So, let me see now.

No, we had Reuben Oliver then. Reuben Oliver was playing. He was a banjo player. Banjo. Oh, man. That same big fellow on bass, I can't get his name. I can't call his name either. Well, thank Kevin. I can't call his name either, cause he was on the boat, but I don't know what it's up. And this boy, trombone player, played sax, one trombone player on one sax, we just call people's names. George, uh, one with the sax and one trombone player, they would sit up on the boat there a while, too. Talk about Nelson, Nelson Jones and Nelson, and Nelson, uh, George Nelson, George Nelson, George
Nelson, George Nelson George Nelson was saxophone player, George Nelson was saxophone player, and Nelson Jones was a trombone player.
And a drummer then would be, uh, well Wills was playing a drummer on a boat with me. with me. Yeah, Will's came on a boat. So, let's see if I got that straight or not.

Chani was there first on the boat? Yeah. And then who took Chani's place? Will's took his place? Yeah, Will's took his place. What's Will's full name? I don't know Will's full name. And this Reuben Oliver, what were you saying about him? Reuben Oliver, does he live near here or something? No, does he know what he's talking about?

Oh, that's uh, Rice Blair between Onzag and La Perouse. We'll have to look for him too. He's out of the... He waits for a sudden demolition. He's out of the trouble. He don't come here. Yeah, but he probably have some good memories. Oh, yeah. How old are you? How old are you? I'm eight, huh? I'm old at nine. I'm going to be married. What? You think he's older than you, Dick? Yeah, he's older than 50. I'm 55. Oh, yeah. He's older than 55. I'm close now. Over 50. I'm 55. I'm 56. I guess.
